title: Is EQ the secret to success
paragraphs: According to research studies coming out of top US universities, having high emotional intelligence, or EQ, can help you to succeed, particularly at work.

The idea of emotional intelligence was introduced by psychologist John Mayer in the 90s and has gained popularity since, especially because it is said to be something that you can improve. Someone with high emotional intelligence can supposedly build strong relationships, achieve their goals and manage their emotions – key areas for success in most jobs!

It’s likely that, during your career, you will need to work in a team. A 2020 Harvard study, published by the National Bureau of Economic Research, investigated social skills and team players. They did this by grouping volunteers and giving them a variety of tricky problems. They then compared the top individual performers. Results showed two main reasons why these individuals excelled, both linked to emotional intelligence. The first reason was that they were very good at recognising the emotional state of their teammates. The second was that they helped to improve their team’s performance through motivation.

When researching links between emotion-understanding ability and risk-taking, a 2012 Yale study found emotional intelligence to be critical to decision making. Researchers investigated the way that leaders come to a decision when they are under pressure. The results revealed that participants with a high awareness of why they felt under pressure managed to keep a clearer head and were less likely to take risks. Being able to understand and manage emotions is a key part of EQ. So, if you’re trying to succeed, work on your emotional intelligence and it may just make a difference!

vocabulary.entry: emotional intelligence (EQ) /ɪˌməʊʃənl ɪnˈtelɪdʒəns/ 情商
vocabulary.example: Emotional intelligence is crucial for building good interpersonal relationships.
vocabulary.translation: 情商对建立良好的人际关系至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: gain popularity /ɡeɪn ˌpɒpjuˈlærəti/ 变得流行；受到欢迎
vocabulary.example: The new style of painting has gained popularity among young artists.
vocabulary.translation: 这种新的绘画风格在年轻艺术家中变得流行起来。

vocabulary.entry: manage one's emotions /ˈmænɪdʒ wʌnz ɪˈməʊʃnz/ 管理自身情绪
vocabulary.example: It's an important life skill to learn how to manage your emotions in difficult situations.
vocabulary.translation: 学会在困境中管理自身情绪是一项重要的生活技能。

vocabulary.entry: social skill /ˈsəʊʃl skɪl/ 社交能力
vocabulary.example: Attending group activities is a good way to develop your social skills.
vocabulary.translation: 参加集体活动是培养社交能力的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: team player /ˈtiːm pleɪə(r)/ 善于团队协作的人；团队合作者
vocabulary.example: The company is looking for a reliable team player for the marketing department.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司正在为市场部招聘一名可靠的团队合作者。

vocabulary.entry: investigate /ɪnˈvestɪɡeɪt/ v. 调查；研究；探究
vocabulary.example: Researchers will investigate the effects of the new drug on human health.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员将调查这种新药对人体健康的影响。

vocabulary.entry: tricky problem /ˈtrɪki ˈprɒbləm/ 棘手的问题
vocabulary.example: We need to hold a meeting to discuss how to solve this tricky problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要开个会讨论如何解决这个棘手的问题。

vocabulary.entry: individual performer /ˌɪndɪˈvɪdʒuəl pəˈfɔːmə(r)/ 独立执行者；个人表现者
vocabulary.example: He is an excellent individual performer, but he needs to learn to work in a team.
vocabulary.translation: 他是一名出色的独立执行者，但还需要学习团队协作。

vocabulary.entry: excel /ɪkˈsel/ v. 表现出色；擅长；优于他人
vocabulary.example: She excels at playing the piano and has won many competitions.
vocabulary.translation: 她钢琴弹得极好，赢得了许多比赛。

vocabulary.entry: recognise the emotional state /ˈrekəɡnaɪz ði ɪˌməʊʃənl steɪt/ 识别情绪状态
vocabulary.example: A good teacher can quickly recognise the emotional state of their students.
vocabulary.translation: 一名优秀的老师能快速识别学生的情绪状态。

vocabulary.entry: motivation /ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃn/ n. 积极性；激励；动机；推动力
vocabulary.example: The coach's words gave the team a huge boost in motivation.
vocabulary.translation: 教练的话极大地激发了团队的积极性。

vocabulary.entry: emotion-understanding ability /ɪˌməʊʃn ˌʌndəˈstændɪŋ əˈbɪləti/ 情绪理解能力
vocabulary.example: This training course is designed to improve your emotion-understanding ability.
vocabulary.translation: 这门培训课程旨在提升你的情绪理解能力。

vocabulary.entry: risk-taking /ˈrɪsk teɪkɪŋ/ n. 冒险行为；冒险精神；敢于冒险
vocabulary.example: Some level of risk-taking is necessary for starting a new business.
vocabulary.translation: 创业需要一定程度的冒险精神。

vocabulary.entry: critical to /ˈkrɪtɪkl tuː/ 对……至关重要；对……有决定性作用
vocabulary.example: Effective communication is critical to the success of the project.
vocabulary.translation: 有效的沟通对这个项目的成功至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: decision making /dɪˈsɪʒn ˈmeɪkɪŋ/ 决策；制定决策；决策能力
vocabulary.example: The manager is responsible for the final decision making of the department.
vocabulary.translation: 经理负责部门的最终决策。

vocabulary.entry: under pressure /ˈʌndə ˈpreʃə(r)/ 处于压力之下；承受压力
vocabulary.example: Most people perform less well when they are under pressure.
vocabulary.translation: 大多数人在压力之下表现会变差。

vocabulary.entry: reveal /rɪˈviːl/ v. 揭示；显示；透露；暴露
vocabulary.example: The survey results reveal a growing dissatisfaction among young people.
vocabulary.translation: 调查结果揭示了年轻人中日益增长的不满情绪。

vocabulary.entry: keep a clearer head /kiːp ə ˈklɪərə hed/ 保持头脑清醒
vocabulary.example: It's important to keep a clearer head when facing an emergency.
vocabulary.translation: 面对紧急情况时，保持头脑清醒至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: work on /wɜːk ɒn/ 致力于；培养（技能、能力等）；从事于
vocabulary.example: She has been working on her public speaking skills for months.
vocabulary.translation: 她几个月来一直致力于培养自己的公开演讲能力。

vocabulary.entry: make a difference /meɪk ə ˈdɪfrəns/ 产生影响；起作用；带来改变
vocabulary.example: Small changes in your daily life can make a big difference to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 日常生活中的微小改变能对你的健康产生巨大影响。

sentences.english: According to research studies coming out of top US universities, having high emotional intelligence, or EQ, can help you to succeed, particularly at work.
sentences.chinese: 据美国顶尖大学的相关研究表明，拥有高情商（EQ）有助于个人取得成功，尤其是在工作领域。

sentences.english: The idea of emotional intelligence was introduced by psychologist John Mayer in the 90s and has gained popularity since, especially because it is said to be something that you can improve.
sentences.chinese: 情商这一概念由心理学家约翰·迈尔于20世纪90年代提出，此后便逐渐受到广泛关注。这主要是因为，情商被认为是一种可以后天提升的能力。

sentences.english: Someone with high emotional intelligence can supposedly build strong relationships, achieve their goals and manage their emotions – key areas for success in most jobs!
sentences.chinese: 据称，高情商的人能够建立稳固的人际关系、实现个人目标并管理自身情绪，而这些都是大多数工作岗位中取得成功的关键要素。

sentences.english: It’s likely that, during your career, you will need to work in a team.
sentences.chinese: 在你的职业生涯中，很可能需要参与团队协作。

sentences.english: A 2020 Harvard study, published by the National Bureau of Economic Research, investigated social skills and team players. They did this by grouping volunteers and giving them a variety of tricky problems.
sentences.chinese: 美国国家经济研究局于2020年发布了一项哈佛大学的研究，该研究围绕社交技能与团队合作者展开调查。

sentences.english: They then compared the top individual performers. Results showed two main reasons why these individuals excelled, both linked to emotional intelligence.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员将志愿者分组，并为他们设置了一系列棘手的问题，随后对表现最为出色的个体进行了对比分析。

sentences.english: The first reason was that they were very good at recognising the emotional state of their teammates.
sentences.chinese: 结果显示，这些佼佼者之所以脱颖而出，主要有两个原因，且均与情商密切相关。

sentences.english: The second was that they helped to improve their team’s performance through motivation.
sentences.chinese: 第一，他们擅长识别队友的情绪状态；第二，他们通过激励的方式助力团队提升整体表现。

sentences.english: When researching links between emotion-understanding ability and risk-taking, a 2012 Yale study found emotional intelligence to be critical to decision making.
sentences.chinese: 耶鲁大学2012年在一项探究情绪理解能力与冒险行为关联性的研究中发现，情商对决策制定起着至关重要的作用。

sentences.english: Researchers investigated the way that leaders come to a decision when they are under pressure. The results revealed that participants with a high awareness of why they felt under pressure managed to keep a clearer head and were less likely to take risks.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员观察了领导者在面临压力时的决策方式，结果显示，那些能够清晰意识到自身压力来源的参与者，往往能保持头脑清醒，且更不容易做出冒险的决定。

sentences.english: Being able to understand and manage emotions is a key part of EQ.
sentences.chinese: 能够理解并管理情绪，是情商的核心组成部分。

sentences.english: So, if you’re trying to succeed, work on your emotional intelligence and it may just make a difference!
sentences.chinese: 因此，如果你渴望取得成功，不妨着力提升自己的情商——这或许会带来意想不到的改变。
